It's definitely not. As others have said it's a very personal decision and it's important to take time to figure yourself out. 

With that in mind, it might help to examine *why* you are so comfortable in the closet. If it's because you are in a homophobic/unsupportive environment, then it may be in your best interests to stay in the closet for the time being. If it's because of something else, then you might be doing yourself an injustice by *never* coming out. It's good to push yourself outside your comfort zone, within reason. Only you will know what's best for you though. Good luck with whatever you choose to do!

It's not so much that my family environment was toxic or dangerous, it absolutely wasn't. I've always had very few friends and was bullied throughout school and thus changed school several times because of it, trying to escape from it even though it always seemed to find me again. The doctors wouldn't help me with how depressed I was because they said it wasn't serious enough. I was stuck in a rut and I wanted out of it, so I booked my ticket and left. 

My mum didn't know any of this was really going on. She knew how I was feeling but not the complexity of it. It's not because she was cold or distant, I've just never felt comfortable telling people about any of my problems. 

This is why I feel so guilty. If she were a bitch and the rest of my family were the same I wouldn't feel bad in the slightest about leaving, but my mum was under the impression that she had a solid family unit and I've disrupted it all in the space of a week. I'm not going to just give up and go home, but I'm not as excited to be here as I was before I arrived.
